_meta.notes: Youth unemployment (ages 15–34 and 15–24) from QLFS Q2 2026 (published 2026-08-11). 15–24 values are published in Table 2.2. 15–34 Q2 2026 (47.4%) and Q1 2026 (45.9%, implied by the official +1.5 pp change) are stated by Stats SA; 15–34 for Q2–Q4 2025 are DERIVED from Table 2.2 counts (unemployed 15–24 + 25–34 over labour force 15–24 + 25–34), rounded to 0.1. REVIEW REQUIRED: (1) youth-unemployment-expanded is unchanged — Stats SA stopped reporting the expanded rate after Q2 2025, so its Q3–Q4 2025 values cannot be traced to an official release; (2) youth-neet-rate is the quarterly NEET rate for 15–24 from QLFS Q4 2025 (34.0%, section 4.2, page 8; series from Table 7b, page 82), shown as the maintainer asked on 2026-10-28; QLFS Q2 2026 prints 36.4% (page 8); (3) series points before Q2 2025 were not re-verified.
_meta.public_notes: Youth unemployment for ages 15 to 34 and 15 to 24, from QLFS Q2 2026 (published 11 August 2026), Table 2.2. The 15 to 34 rate is calculated by SA Data Hub from the published counts for ages 15 to 24 and 25 to 34, as are its values for Q2 to Q4 2025. The NEET rate for youth aged 15–24 years is from QLFS Q4 2025 (published 17 February 2026), page 8 and Table 7b, page 82. The expanded youth unemployment rate is not shown: Stats SA does not publish an expanded rate in the QLFS releases SA Data Hub holds. Points before Q2 2025 have not yet been rechecked.

statistics.title: Youth unemployment rate, ages 15 to 34
statistics.description: Narrow (strict) unemployment rate for those aged 15–34 who are without work, available for work and actively seeking employment. Stats SA reports the rate rose 1.5 percentage points to 47.4% in Q2 2026; the number of unemployed youth rose by 264,000 to 5.0 million.

statistics.title: Youth unemployment rate, ages 15 to 24
statistics.description: Unemployment rate (LU1) among 15–24 year olds, one of the highest youth rates in the world. It rose 1.9 percentage points to 62.8% in Q2 2026. This cohort faces structural barriers including lack of experience, skills mismatch, and geographic concentration of youth outside economic centres.

statistics.title: Expanded youth unemployment rate, ages 15 to 34
statistics.description: The expanded youth unemployment rate also counts discouraged work-seekers: people who want work but have stopped actively looking for it.

statistics.title: NEET rate for youth aged 15–24 years
statistics.description: Share of young people aged 15–24 who are not in employment, education or training (NEET). Stats SA: "There were about 10,3 million young people aged 15–24 years in Q4: 2025, of which 34,0% were not in employment, education or training. This is 0,5 of a percentage point higher than the NEET rate in Q4: 2024." (QLFS Q4 2025, page 8).
